blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Accounting is the language of Czarnikow's numbers. Today's topic is simple: Money In and Money Out. Money in is income. Money out is expense. Good accountants keep clear, honest numbers.

You work with the finance team. You check the cash and the bank every day. The income has to match the records. There is one new expense to review this week.

Go slow. One step at a time. That is how good accountants work. You can do it!

items.q: What is "money in"?
items.why: "Money in is income." Income = receita (dinheiro que entra).

items.q: How often do you check the cash and the bank?
items.why: "You check the cash and the bank every day."

items.q: How many new expenses are there to review this week?
items.why: "There is one new expense to review this week."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with…
options: "It is fine to rush and skip steps."
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz "Go slow. One step at a time." — ele não concorda com pressa.

items.q: The words "You can do it!" suggest that the text wants to…
items.why: Inferência: o tom é de apoio e incentivo ao novo colaborador.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie apresentar o tema para um novo trainee. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi, welcome to the team. My name is Sophie. I help new trainees here.

Today we start with money. It is easy. Money in is income. Money out is expense. Say it with me: income, expense. Good.

Look at this desk. There is a small box of cash here. And there is a laptop for the bank. Every day, we check the cash. Every day, we check the bank too. There are two simple jobs, and you can do both.

The income has to match the records. That is the rule. Numbers must be clear and honest. There is one new expense to review this week. It is on your desk.

Do not worry. Go slow. One step at a time. When you finish, leave the account on my desk, please. Our team is small, but we are very organised. You can do it. Ready for the next step?
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is Sophie's job?
options: She sells cash to the bank
items.why: "My name is Sophie. I help new trainees here."

items.q: What two things are on the desk?
options: A box of coins and a book
A box of cash and a laptop for the bank
items.why: "There is a small box of cash here. And there is a laptop for the bank."

items.q: How many new expenses are there to review this week?
items.why: "There is one new expense to review this week."

items.q: Why does Sophie say "Say it with me: income, expense"?
options: She wants the trainee to practise and remember
items.why: Inferência: ela usa repetição para ajudar o iniciante a fixar o vocabulário.

items.q: How would you best describe Sophie's tone?
items.why: Inferência: "Do not worry. Go slow… You can do it." — ela é tranquila e incentiva.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Our income this month is good." Income means…
items.why: Income = receita, o dinheiro que entra.

items.q: "Coffee and paper are a small expense." An expense is…
items.why: Expense = despesa, o dinheiro que sai.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "There is some ___ in the box for small payments."
items.why: Cash = dinheiro/caixa (notas e moedas), o que fica na caixinha.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We keep the money safe in the ___."
items.why: Bank = banco, onde o dinheiro fica guardado.

items.q: "Please leave the account on my desk." Here, an account is…
items.why: Account = conta, um registro de dinheiro (entradas e saídas).

blocks.instruction: Expressões simples que aparecem no dia a dia da equipe de finanças. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager has to sign off on the expense." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar, dar o aval.

items.q: "Let's go over the numbers together." To go over means to…
items.why: Go over = revisar, checar com atenção.

items.q: "The bank total does not add up." To add up means the numbers…
items.why: Add up = bater, fechar direito. "Does not add up" = não bate.

items.q: "Can you write down the new expense?" To write down means to…
items.why: Write down = anotar, registrar por escrito.

items.q: "We are on track with the records this week." On track means…
items.why: On track = no caminho certo, dentro do planejado.
